findings.message: Redaction now only matches exact key names from SENSITIVE_FIELDS, so sensitive values under differently-named or differently-cased keys (e.g. 'access_token', 'api_key', 'client_secret', 'Authorization', 'PASSWORD_HASH') are copied verbatim into the audit log. This silently leaks secrets that were previously redacted.
findings.suggestion: Normalize keys (lowercase/strip) and match by suffix/substring or a broader rule set (e.g. any key containing 'token', 'secret', 'password', 'key', 'auth', 'ssn', 'card', 'cvv', 'otp') before deciding to keep the value; fail closed by redacting unknown keys if audit logs must be safe by default.
